subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a global `openclaw agent --dry-run` mode, and which tool-execution surfaces must be covered before users can trust it as side-effect-free?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the safety boundary would define public CLI behavior and security semantics across multiple runtime and delegation paths.

options.title: Define the safety contract first
options.body: Specify covered surfaces, preview payloads, hook/approval ordering, read-only exceptions, redaction, and unsupported paths before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader workflow modes
options.body: Keep this issue as the focused tool-preview requirement while coordinating terminology and scope with the broader Ask/Plan/Modify tracker.

options.title: Decline global dry-run
options.body: Keep command-specific dry-runs and tool policy hooks as the supported safety model, then close this direction by maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Define the safety contract first
recommendation.body: Specify covered surfaces, preview payloads, hook/approval ordering, read-only exceptions, redaction, and unsupported paths before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for both the shared tool adapter and Gateway-first agent CLI dispatch boundary.
